For this benchmark, store paired per-user hit indicators for both models on identical users and fixed candidates. Compute Δ = ¼Σ_d mean_u(hit_new − hit_baseline). Bootstrap 200 users with replacement independently within each dataset, preserving model pairs; recompute the four-dataset macro difference for each replicate. Use, for example, 10,000 replicates with a recorded bootstrap seed and report Δ, its 95% percentile interval, and category differences. Bootstrap users, never candidate items or four dataset scores; directly estimate the difference rather than compare overlapping model intervals. One changed hit moves macro HR@10 by 0.125 percentage points. This applies the [paired-bootstrap principle](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html) to the benchmark’s fixed strata.

Prespecify checkpoint evaluation frequency, selection rule, tie-breaking and search budget; apply comparable rules to both methods. Log every checkpoint/trial comparison. Selecting the best checkpoint and then bootstrapping its validation predictions does not account for selection optimism. Treat these intervals as exploratory after adaptive search. For a prespecified finite comparison family, use multiplicity control such as Holm-adjusted valid p-values; ordinary corrections do not automatically validate adaptive model invention. Freeze the final selection before the host’s held-out evaluation, without changing pinned splits. These precautions address [model-selection bias](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html) and [adaptive holdout reuse](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02629).

With training seed 42 alone, intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the fitted models and fixed benchmark. They cannot establish robustness across initialization, training order, sampling, splits or search runs; that requires repeated training. Fixed negative candidates also leave candidate-sampling uncertainty unmeasured, and sampled HR@10 need not preserve full-catalog rankings. Report these limits explicitly ([training variance](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.03098); [sampled recommendation metrics](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).
